My family has worked this land in Quzhou my whole life. No school, but I've been farming since I was a boy watching my father. I know this soil, I know the seasons here.

The decision is simple — I plant wheat in autumn, corn after the wheat comes off. That's the rotation. Everyone around here does it, and it's worked for generations. I have about 10 mu of contracted land. I'll put all of it into the wheat-corn double crop. Maybe keep half a mu near the house for vegetables for the family, but that's not really "farming," that's just the kitchen garden.

For wheat, I'll buy Jimai-series seeds from the seed shop in town. Not traditional saved seed — I stopped that years ago because yields were falling — but I won't go chasing some new variety either. Stick with what I know works here. I'll rotary till after the corn is harvested, put down compound fertilizer when I sow, then come back with urea when the wheat is jointing in spring.

Irrigation worries me more every year. The well is deeper than it used to be. But I won't cut corners on the wheat water — I'll do pre-sowing moisture, winter water, jointing water, and filling water. Four times. That's what it needs here.

For corn, I always buy hybrid seed —郑单 or 先玉 type, whatever the shop has that others are using. I direct-seed into the wheat stubble, no tillage. Corn doesn't need as much water in summer because there's more rain. Two irrigations should be enough unless it's a dry year.

Pesticides — I'll spray herbicide early, and come back for rust and aphids on the wheat at heading. For corn, herbicide after emergence and one spray for borers if I see them bad.
